Best Chocolate Chip Cookies

4.6
(19,332)
14,911 Reviews
4,925 Photos

This chocolate chip cookie recipe makes dozens of delicious cookies with crisp edges, chewy centers, and plenty of chocolate chips.

Submitted by Dora
Updated on October 5, 2026
Tested by

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

  • A generous batch makes this recipe perfect for parties, cookie swaps, and holiday trays.
  • Home cooks love customizing them with walnuts, pecans, or different chocolate chips.
  • Freeze baked cookies or portioned dough to enjoy fresh-baked treats anytime.

This chocolate chip cookie recipe makes dozens of cookies with crisp edges, chewy centers, and melty chocolate chips. It is truly the best! With more than 14,000 rave reviews from the Allrecipes community, this top-rated chocolate chip cookie recipe will quickly become your go-to for every occasion.

Chocolate Chip Cookies Ingredients

Here’s what you’ll need to make the best chocolate chip cookies:

  • Butter: Softened butter blends easily with the sugars and creates a smooth dough. Salted or unsalted butter will work.
  • Sugars: A combination of white and brown sugar gives the cookies their balanced flavor and texture.
  • Eggs and vanilla: Eggs bind the dough, while vanilla adds flavor.
  • Baking soda, hot water, and salt: These pantry staples help the cookies bake properly and balance the sweetness.
  • Flour: Use all-purpose flour and measure it carefully to avoid dry cookies.
  • Chocolate chips: Semisweet chocolate chips provide classic flavor, but milk or dark chocolate chips also work.
  • Walnuts: The nuts are optional. Substitute chopped pecans, if preferred.

Test Kitchen Tips

“Everyone needs a good chocolate chip cookie recipe,” says culinary producer Nicole McLaughlin (a.k.a. NicoleMcMom). Here are a few of her expert tips and tricks for making perfect chocolate chip cookies every time: 

  • Beating the butter and sugar is the most important part of the chocolate chip cookie-making process, according to Nicole. It takes a lot longer than you might think: She recommends beating the ingredients together for about four minutes.
  • Nicole suggests chilling the dough before baking to prevent spreading. This is essential if you want a cookie that’s still a little gooey in the middle, she says. 
  • Remove the cookies when the edges are lightly browned and the centers are just set. They will continue to firm up on the baking sheet. Let them rest briefly before moving them to a wire rack so they don’t break apart.

How to Store Chocolate Chip Cookies

Store the cooled chocolate chip cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to a week. If you want to go the extra mile, throw a piece of white bread into the container — it’ll absorb the dry air and keep the cookies soft for longer.

Learn more: How to Store Cookies So They Stay Fresh

Can You Freeze Chocolate Chip Cookies?

Yes! You can freeze baked chocolate chip cookies and chocolate chip cookie dough.

  • To freeze baked cookies: Allow the baked cookies to cool completely. Arrange them in a single layer on a baking sheet, cover, and freeze for about three hours or up to overnight. Transfer the now-frozen cookies to a resealable plastic freezer bag or freezer-safe container. Wrap in at least one layer of aluminum foil for extra protection. Freeze for up to two months.
  • To freeze cookie dough: Drop balls of dough onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover and freeze for about three hours or up to overnight. Transfer the frozen cookie dough balls to a resealable plastic freezer bag or freezer-safe container. Wrap in at least one layer of aluminum foil for extra protection. Freeze for up to two months.

Learn more: How to Freeze Cookies and Cookie Dough for Easy Baking

Allrecipes Community Tips and Praise

“My go-to recipe,” says Andrea Howard. “I sometimes add oatmeal, nuts, raisins, etc. but they are also fantastic without. Crunchy and chewy in every bite!”

“This is hands down the best chocolate chip cookie recipe!” raves Baybos the baker man. “So good that we want to quadruple the recipe and freeze a few batches.”

“I decided to give this recipe a try,” says another reviewer. “I have been making chocolate chip cookies for my family for years and this recipe turned out to be the best for cookies ever! I usually add about 2 and a half cups of chocolate chips because it gives it that gooey, chocolatey taste that I think chocolate chip cookies need.”

Ingredients

Oops! Something went wrong. Our team is working on it.

This recipe was developed at its original yield. Ingredient amounts are automatically adjusted, but cooking times and steps remain unchanged. Note that not all recipes scale perfectly. Original recipe (1X) yields 48 servings

  • 1 cup butter, softened

  • 1 cup white sugar

  • 1 cup packed brown sugar

  • 2 large eggs

  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract

  • 1 teaspoon baking soda

  • 2 teaspoons hot water

  • ½ teaspoon salt

  • 3 cups all-purpose flour

  • 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips

  • 1 cup chopped walnuts

Directions

  1. Gather your ingredients, making sure your butter is softened, and your eggs are room temperature.

  2. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and creamy, about 4 minutes.

  3. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla.

  4. Dissolve baking soda in hot water; add to batter along with salt and mix until combined.

  5. Stir in flour just until no dry streaks remain. Fold in chocolate chips and walnuts, if using, until evenly distributed.

  6. Drop rounded 1 ½-tablespoon portions of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets, using a medium cookie scoop if desired.

  7. Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are lightly browned and the centers are just set, about 10 minutes.

  8. Let the cookies cool briefly on the baking sheets, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.

  9. Serve or store cooled cookies in an airtight container.

Tips

The walnuts are optional. You can leave them out or substitute chopped pecans.

If the dough feels very soft or the first batch spreads too much, chill the remaining dough until it is firm enough to scoop.

To get ahead, scoop the dough onto a baking sheet and freeze until firm. Transfer the portions to a freezer-safe container and freeze for up to two months. Thaw in the refrigerator before baking as directed.
